name: Technical Surveillance Countermeasures
description: Ability to conduct technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) inspections to detect covert surveillance devices. Covers RF spectrum sweeps for active transmitters, non-linear junction detection (NLJD) for electronic components, physical inspection methodology, telephone and wiring analysis, thermal and power-line analysis, and assessment of facility technical security posture.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to technical surveillance countermeasures

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands TSCM threat landscape and inspection methodology concepts
evidence: Can describe common covert surveillance device types (RF, GSM, WiFi, audio, video)
Understands the TSCM inspection methodology phases (RF survey, physical, electronic, reporting)
Completed training on TSCM fundamentals and threat awareness

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Assists in TSCM inspections and operates detection equipment under supervision
evidence: Conducted RF spectrum sweeps for anomalous transmissions under guidance
Operated non-linear junction detector (NLJD) on target areas under supervision
Assisted with physical inspection of fixtures, furnishings, and building elements

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently conducts TSCM inspections of standard office and meeting room environments
evidence: Independently conducted TSCM inspections for 3+ facilities
Identified and characterized anomalous RF emissions during spectrum sweeps
Conducted systematic physical and electronic inspection of target spaces
Produced TSCM inspection reports documenting methodology, findings, and risk assessment

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Inspects high-security facilities; detects sophisticated devices; develops inspection methodology
evidence: Conducted TSCM inspections of high-security or sensitive compartmented facilities
Detected sophisticated surveillance devices including burst transmitters and carrier-current devices
Performed telephone and structured cabling analysis for surveillance taps
Mentors junior TSCM inspectors and reviews inspection reports

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines TSCM methodology; designs technical security programs; recognized surveillance detection authority
evidence: Authored the lab's TSCM inspection methodology and equipment standards
Designed ongoing technical security monitoring programs for sensitive facilities
Evaluated emerging surveillance technologies and updated detection methodologies accordingly
Trains TSCM inspection teams and provides expert testimony on surveillance detection

assessment_methods.description: Conduct a TSCM inspection of a prepared lab space containing planted surveillance devices, documenting all findings and detection methodology
Review TSCM inspection reports for methodology completeness, detection coverage, and risk assessment quality

equipment: Keysight N9040B or equivalent real-time spectrum analyzer
